findings.summary: NoteIn.text has minLength 1 but no maxLength, so the note text has no upper bound on size.
GET /api/notes returns the full NoteList with no pagination, limit, or ordering parameter, so one request can return every note.
POST /api/invite declares no 400 response, although Invite.email has format email; the response to a malformed address is not specified.
POST /api/invite is secured with bearer auth but declares no 401 response.
Note creation (201) is specified with a webhook notification, but the spec gives no outcome when the webhook call fails after the note is stored.
No route or schema in the index or source implements the webhook notification; the spec only shows a note-creation response.
Account creation, login, note listing, reading and deletion routes exist but the brief never mentions them.
Note read and delete routes take a Note with an owner field but declare no 403 response and no ownership rule, so whether a user may act on another user's note is unspecified.
Credentials.username and password have minLength 1 but no maxLength, and POST /api/users declares 409 for duplicates without stating which field is unique.
Session has no expiry field, so token lifetime and behaviour after expiry are not specified.
